facts.writers: Several agents (phone, tablet, cloud sessions) commit to the vault; git merges their changes through pull requests.

options.custom_harness: The operator's planned system. Third-party stacks are broken into assets and only the useful parts are folded in. Claude Code is the harness, customised with hooks, skills, subagents and mods. Routing is a UserPromptSubmit hook that asks Jev typed questions and sends unsure cases to a Sonnet or Opus subagent. Episodic memory is a Stop hook where Jev decides what to keep and appends it to a markdown file in the repo. Semantic retrieval uses the vault, its manifest and per-section Jev labels, with grep and Jev relevance ranking. Graphify and code-review-graph stay as the graph layers. Everything is files in git; no extra database servers. Much of it is not built yet.
options.third_party_servers: Run the third-party servers whole, as their projects ship them: OmniRoute as a localhost gateway that every prompt passes through, with its own SQLite store; mem0 for episodic memory with Postgres and Neo4j; OB1 / Terrestrial Brain on Supabase or Postgres with pgvector and LLM-based schema routing; plus Graphify and code-review-graph. Runs in Docker Compose on the GCP VM, reached from the phone over Tailscale. The operator earlier found OB1 intrusive and said it attempts to hijack prompts.
options.baseline_claude_code: Plain Claude Code with no additions: it reads AGENTS.md and the files it is pointed at, uses its built-in memory files and subagents, and searches the vault with grep when asked. No Jev, no routing layer, no memory servers, no graph tools.
